title: Analog Circuits and Semiconductor Devices
description: This course covers analog circuits, including: amplifiers, oscillators, and filters, using single-chip analog devices, operational amplifiers, field-effect transistors, bipolar transistors.
outcomes: Identify op-amp circuit configurations and calculate gain and impedances for the circuit
Identify the terminals and basic internal construction of MOSFETs, and describe the operation of MOSFET switching and amplifier circuits.
objectives: 1. Transistors: Demonstrate the understanding of how general and specific (Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT), MOSFET) transistors work and can be used in application circuits
2. Amplifiers: Identify and draw basic amplifier circuits
3. Operational-Amplifier: Demonstrate the understanding of the specifications and applications of an op-amp.
4. Oscillators: Demonstrate the understanding of common types of oscillators, recognize their schematic symbols, and how they are used in circuit applications
5. Power Amplifiers: Demonstrate the understanding of how transistors are used in power amplifiers
content: Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (MOSFET)
Op Amp Amplifiers and closed-loop configurations
lab: Basics of circuits through the creation and simulation of resistor based circuits.
AC signals and corresponding circuits that include capacitors and inductors
Filters and time constants - including the use of scopes to visualize the impact of the filters.
Measure and compare the performance of different classes of amplifiers including classes AB and D with some of the configurations in the following list:
Integrated amplifier, oscillator, and filter devices
assignments: Students are expected to work on homework in order to learn the materials.
Example: Calculate the gain and impedance for an Op-amp circuit with a specific configuration.
Students use the concepts and technical skills learned in the class to analyze and solve practical problems.
Example: Measure and compare the performance of a class AB and class D amplifier, including gain, bandwidth, noise, and efficiency.
Example: Designing a Low-Cost Analog Hearing Aid Preamp Circuit
Students demonstrate their understanding of the materials with written explanation or lab reports.
Example: Develop and execute a troubleshooting plan for a Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (MOSFET) oscillator circuit.
